blocks.title: What is demand?
blocks.md: **Demand** is the quantity of a good or service that people are **willing and able** to buy at a given price during a period. The **law of demand**: when the price falls, people buy more; when the price rises, they buy less. A **demand schedule** is a table of prices and the quantities bought. Drawn as a graph it gives the **demand curve**, which slopes downwards.

blocks.title: What changes demand?
blocks.md: Besides price, demand depends on **income** (more income, more demand for most goods), **tastes and fashion**, **prices of other goods** (if rice becomes dearer, people may buy more garri), the **number of buyers** and **advertising**. A change in price only moves us **along** the same curve; a change in income, tastes or another factor **shifts** the whole curve.

blocks.caption: Demand for puff-puff at five prices: the quantity bought falls as the price rises.
blocks.alt: Five bars labelled with prices 100 to 500 FCFA, decreasing in height from 55 to 15.

blocks.title: Quantity or demand?
blocks.md: If the **price** changes, write that the **quantity demanded** changes. If **income, taste or population** changes, write that **demand** increases or decreases. Do not confuse 'I want it' with demand: demand needs money to pay. A rise in price does not make people stop buying completely, it only reduces the amount.

blocks.title: Reading a demand table
blocks.md: Look down the table: as price goes up, quantity falls. To find the change in quantity between two prices, subtract. To find total spending at a price multiply **price × quantity**. Spending is not always the same at each price, so compare.

blocks.title: Worked example — reading the schedule
blocks.statement: A seller of puff-puff in Kumba records the number bought each day: at 100 FCFA, 55; at 200 FCFA, 45; at 300 FCFA, 35; at 400 FCFA, 25; at 500 FCFA, 15 (illustrative). How many fewer are bought when the price rises from 200 to 400 FCFA?

blocks.title: Worked example — spending
blocks.statement: Using the same table, how much do customers spend in total when the price is 300 FCFA?

blocks.title: Supply and the market price
blocks.md: **Supply** is the quantity sellers are **willing and able to offer** at each price. The **law of supply**: when the price rises, sellers offer more; when it falls, they offer less. The **market price** (equilibrium price) is the price at which the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied. At this price the market is **balanced**: everyone who wants to buy at that price can buy.

blocks.title: Shortage and surplus
blocks.md: If the price is **too low**, buyers want more than sellers offer: a **shortage**. Competing buyers push the price **up**. If the price is **too high**, sellers offer more than buyers want: a **surplus**. Sellers cut the price to sell the extra. The price moves toward the equilibrium. **Shortage = demand − supply**; **surplus = supply − demand** at a given price.

blocks.caption: A market table: balance at 300 FCFA, shortages below it and surpluses above it.
blocks.alt: A table with five prices and columns for demand, supply and result.

blocks.title: What changes supply?
blocks.md: Supply increases when **costs fall** (cheaper seeds, fuel or wages), when **technology** improves, when the **weather** is good for farm products, or when the government gives a **subsidy**. Supply decreases when costs rise, when there is drought, or when a tax is placed on sellers. The new supply shifts the market price.

blocks.title: Do not mix
blocks.md: A price change moves us **along** the curve; a change in costs, weather or technology **shifts** the supply curve. Do not say there is a surplus and a shortage at the same price. Equilibrium does not mean that everyone is happy: it only means demand equals supply.

blocks.title: Worked example — equilibrium
blocks.statement: Use the table: at 200 FCFA demand is 45 and supply is 25; at 300 FCFA, demand 35 and supply 35; at 400 FCFA, demand 25 and supply 45. Find the equilibrium price.
steps: At 300: demand 35 = supply 35, so there is balance.
At 400: supply − demand = 20, a surplus. So the equilibrium price is 300 FCFA.

blocks.title: Worked example — surplus
blocks.statement: Using the same table, find the surplus at 500 FCFA (demand 15, supply 55).
steps: At 500 FCFA the quantity supplied is 55.
Surplus = 55 − 15 = 40. Sellers will cut the price.
